newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: G10 sees growth in 1997 and 1998 - Tietmeyer.
newsitem.headline: G10 sees growth in 1997 and 1998 - Tietmeyer.

text.p: Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer said the latest indicators and forecasts from Group of 10 (G10) countries showed economic growth within the group was strengthening and would accelerate modestly this year and in 1998.
But Tietmeyer also said unemployment remained the most difficult part of the economic situation in continental Europe.

"The latest forecasts continue to suggest a modest acceleration of real growth this year as far as the G10 group is concerned," Tietmeyer told reporters. "It is expected that this acceleration will be sustained in 1998," he added.
Tietmeyer was briefing reporters after the monthly meeting of the G10 central bank governors committee which he chairs.
Tietmeyer said leading indicators in most G10 countries had strengthened recently and forecasts for the G10 as a whole were brighter than they had been in mid-1996.
Tietmeyer said this was the general picture, but that there were differences between growth prospects in individual countries, which he declined to elaborate on.
"The most difficult point is the unemployment situation, especially in continental Europe," Tietmeyer said.
Tietmeyer said unemployment figures were currently rising in most countries in continental Europe.
"This is based on structural reasons," he said.

"Of course strong growth rates will improve the situation, but the growth alone cannot solve it. The structural problems have to be addressed in Europe," Tietmeyer said. -- Zurich Editorial +41 1 631 7340
